title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
An AI music generation system was trained on copyrighted songs without authorization from the rights holders. The system was deployed to users who could generate new music from text prompts, and the training data strategy became apparent only through litigation after the fact. What would have caught this was licensing agreements with rights holders before training began, or at minimum before deployment to the public.

The core failure was building a generative model on unlicensed material. The startup subsequently settled with Universal Music Group and agreed to build a new platform using only authorized music. Sony Music and independent artists pursued separate legal action. Whether the system actually copied or merely resembled existing songs in its outputs is not established by the reporting, though allegations of similarity to specific recordings were made.

summary:
Universal Music Group has reached a settlement with AI music startup Udio, ending a lawsuit that accused the company of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence model. Under the agreement, Udio will launch a new platform next year that only uses authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, and share songs. The specific financial terms were not disclosed. UMG's CEO stated the settlement demonstrates the company's commitment to supporting artists and songwriters while embracing new technology and business models.

The dispute centered on allegations that Udio used popular songs without permission to develop its AI system, which generates original music from text prompts. UMG claimed Udio created a song called "Sunshine Melody" that closely resembled The Temptations' "My Girl," including similar melodies, chords, and backing vocals. This marks Udio's first licensing agreement with a major music label. The startup, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees and backed by notable investors including will.i.am, has attracted millions of users since its launch.
